title: Collection and progression
summary: Experiences where discovering, collecting, improving, displaying, or exchanging owned things supplies a major part of the play loop.

designKnowledge.playerPromise: Players discover objects or beings with identity, make meaningful choices about what to keep or develop, and express or test the resulting collection.
coreLoop: use, improve, trade, or display it
designKnowledge.economy: Define rarity, duplicate handling, sinks, trading constraints, and non-paying paths together. Random rewards require clear odds and a valuable deterministic route to progress.
designKnowledge.multiplayer: Trading and gifting need server-owned ownership, recipient eligibility, duplicate-request protection, and a recoverable transaction record.
designKnowledge.artAndAnimation: Collection entries need distinct silhouettes, readable rarity cues, an inventory grid that scales to touch, and reveal motion that preserves the acquired object's identity.
productRisks: trades that duplicate or destroy value
rarety cues that are inaccessible by color alone

technicalPatterns.name: Server-owned collection ledger
technicalPatterns.guidance: The server validates grants, ownership, transfer eligibility, and duplicate requests. Client UI submits intent and renders the confirmed result.

technicalPatterns.name: Acquisition and use are separate systems
technicalPatterns.guidance: Model how an item is granted separately from where it can be equipped, consumed, upgraded, or traded.

dependencies.rationale: Questing and exploration can provide deterministic acquisition routes and a world context for collection goals.
A collection can become a tactical roster or deck when each entry supports distinct decisions.

failureModes.description: Collected entries differ only in rarity or numeric value and do not change play or expression.
failureModes.mitigation: Review each entry for distinct utility, social expression, visual identity, or collection meaning before expanding the catalog.

failureModes.description: Retries or concurrent requests grant the same reward more than once.
failureModes.mitigation: Use server-side idempotency and test replayed requests, simultaneous clients, and disconnects.

scenarios.action: Retry the same collection acquisition with repeated and concurrent client requests.
scenarios.expected: The server grants at most one valid entry and both clients observe the same confirmed state.

scenarios.action: Test a trade where one participant leaves before confirmation.
scenarios.expected: The transaction either completes once or returns both inventories to their prior authoritative state.

acceptanceCriteria: Players can explain how to earn an early collection entry.
Duplicate entries have a defined purpose or resolution.
Acquisition, exchange, and use are independently testable.

considerations: Bound inventory rendering and avoid loading every model or animation at once.
Profile collection menus on a midrange mobile device with a representative inventory size.

sourceRefs.title: Approved Lab game-family and hybrid scope

evidence.description: Structured collection loop, economy, ownership, failure modes, and repeatable multiplayer acceptance scenarios.

assumptions: This record does not prescribe monetization or a particular randomized acquisition model.
Trading and randomized rewards require separate product, safety, and platform policy review.
